text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London erased their losses in last minute deals before the close. August, which had slumped along with New York, was hovering about $1.30 down until the close when it finished 10 cents firmer at $310.50 per tonne. October finished 30 cents higher at $300.70 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed a heavily-traded session lower. Talk of Russian buying coupled with fears of tight supplies fueled July to a contract high of 11.37 cents/lb on April 23 in spite of warnings that there is enough sugar around to satisfy all requirements. However, the party seems to be over and the market is in for a major correction. The most-active July contract ended 26 points lower at 10.70 cents/lb, while October gave up 22 points to close at 10.60 cents/lb. The outer months closed 7 to 13 points lower. Traders said that with big open interest, July will remain under pressure with a potential to fall to 10.25 to 10.50 cents.

EUROPE - European sugar beet sowings have been very rapid this season due to the drier than normal conditions across the western portion of the continent. Light rainfall at the end of April stabilized moisture conditions although it is still too dry in many areas. Additional rainfall expected during early May could cause a major improvement in moisture conditions, especially in France and the UK where it has been driest. Poland and Germany should recover from the cold weather damage that occurred during mid-April. In Spain, beet regions were mostly dry during the week ended April 30, but conditions have stabilized due to favourable rainfall during the previous week. The eastern European beet areas continued to have favourable moisture for good early growth but growth is being slowed by the cooler than normal weather.

RUSSIA - Sugar beet sowings are behind those of last year. The total sown reached 180,000 ha by April 28, 25 per cent down from the 240,000 ha sown the same date last year. The delay coupled with the cooler than normal weather could have a negative impact on yields, although it is still too early to make any firm predictions.

POLAND - Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 108,411 tonnes, raw value, sharply up from last year's 348 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first four months of 1996/97 (September/December) up to 175,090 tonnes compared to 1,801 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached no more than 4,440 tonnes against 14,828 tonnes in 1994/95 and 216,600 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in September/December 1996 were Algeria with 25,303 tonnes whites against nil, Germany with 25,063 tonnes compared to nil, Syria with 28,189 tonnes raws and Algeria with 18,450 tonnes raws compared to 206 tonnes.

Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 9,273 tonnes, up from 490 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in September/December 1996 up to 30,519 tonnes, down from 56,615 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 hit 85,306 tonnes compared to 100,248 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in September/December 1996 were Germany with 11,297 tonnes whites against 8,343 tonnes, the Czech Republic with 7,836 tonnes whites against nil and 4,542 tonnes raws against nil.

DENMARK - Sugar beet sowings in Denmark started around April 1 and were completed around April 21. Germination is satisfactory although low temperatures in April have caused some delays. Temperatures in the week ended April 27 were 1- 3 C below normal while rainfall amounts in April ranged between 15-39 mm compared to an average of 34-36 mm. The overall crop outlook is reported to be normal.

CANADA - Sugar imports in January 1997 amounted to 31,701 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from last year's 73,976 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 461,117 tonnes compared to 403,698 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.160 mn tonnes compared to 1.013 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/January 1996/97 were Australia with 382,404 tonnes raws against 328,299 tonnes, Brazil with 53,578 tonnes against 24,500 tonnes and Cuba with 16,571 tonnes, up from 7,500 tonnes.

Sugar exports in October/January 1996/97 amounted to 10,192 tonnes, down from 18,081 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 36,420 tonnes compared to 43,198 tonnes in 1994/95. Canada exports most of its white sugar to the USA (8,131 vs 15,291 tonnes).

The European Union awarded 34,500 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.069 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on April 30. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to April 30 reached 1,905,050 tonnes, which compares to 2,006,298 tonnes last year.
